images.title: Touch, miss or cross
images.purpose: Show the three cases for two circles on a base: touch, miss, cross.
images.composition: Three equal panels side by side, each with a horizontal base and two circles, plenty of space between panels.
exact_structure: Left panel: base AB of 8 units in teal (#0072B2), an amber (#E69F00) circle of radius 3 at A and a reddish purple (#CC79A7) circle of radius 5 at B, touching at exactly one point on AB. Caption: touch.
Middle panel: the same base, an amber (#E69F00) circle of radius 2 at A and a reddish purple (#CC79A7) circle of radius 5 at B, with a visible gap of 1 unit between them on AB. Caption: miss.
Right panel: the same base, an amber (#E69F00) circle of radius 5 at A and a reddish purple (#CC79A7) circle of radius 6 at B overlapping and crossing at two points. Caption: cross.
Under each panel one short line: 3 + 5 = 8, 2 + 5 = 7, 5 + 6 = 11.
A green (#009E73) tick under the right panel only and vermilion (#D55E00) crosses under the left and middle panels, showing a triangle exists only for cross.
rejection: any panel showing the wrong case
sums that do not match the circles' radii
a tick under touch or miss
any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Only when the two radii add to more than the base do the circles cross and give a triangle.
images.description: Three panels showing circles that touch, miss and cross, with their radius sums.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Compare each sum with 8 and read off the case.

image_decisions.why: The three cases are the heart of the concept and read best side by side.
